lines: A ledger has gone missing from the village hall. It records every debt and favor in Bellwater for the last twenty years.
Without it, the whole settlement's obligations unravel. I need someone outside the village politics to find it.
Mara told you about the clay pits. Of course she did. She was always the clever one.
The kiln lease was supposed to go to the pottery — that was the promise. But Brand offered me a way to save the village from debt.
I broke my word to my own sister to keep Bellwater alive. The ledger proves it.
Jory has it. He's been blackmailing me with it for months.
You found the burnt letter. The promise was real. Legally binding. I knew. I've known for years.
Brand found out and used it. He said if I signed the kiln lease over to him, he'd cancel the village's debt.
I chose the village over my sister. Over my father's word.
The ledger... Jory has it at the old shrine. Take it. Expose me. I deserve it.
But think on this: if the clay pits go back to the pottery, Brand calls in the debt. The kiln closes. Half the village loses their livelihood.
Sometimes keeping a promise destroys everything else.
I... I have failed you. All of you. My father's name, my sister's trust, this village's honor.
The clay pits belong to the pottery. They always did. I will sign the transfer today.
As for the reeve's seat... I cannot hold it. Not after this.
Mara... if you can find it in your heart to forgive me... I am your brother. I always was.
So. It ends like this. In chains, in my own hall.
I did what I thought was right. For the village. For all of you.
Mara... take the pits. Run the pottery. Do what I couldn't.
Just... don't let Brand win. That's all I ask.
The ledger? Missing? No, I... I must have misplaced it. It'll turn up.
You've done good work. The village is stable. That's what matters.
Mara? She's... she's doing well at the pottery. Family is complicated, isn't it?
Thank you. For looking into this. Bellwater is fortunate to have you.
Edric sent you? Figures. He and I haven't spoken in three years, not since the kiln deal.
That ledger... it's not just accounts. It's the promise he broke.
Ask him about the kiln lease. Ask him who really owns the clay pits.
You found the letter. Father's own hand. 'The clay pits shall pass to the potter's line.'
All these years... I thought I'd failed. Thought my work wasn't good enough.
And it was him. My brother. Stealing my birthright to pay off Brand.
The pottery... we can finally expand. Hire apprentices. Be what it was meant to be.
Edric... you stood in the square and told everyone the truth. That took courage I didn't think you had.
The clay pits are mine. Ours. The pottery will thrive.
But I don't want the reeve's seat. A council... yes. We'll build something better together.
Brother. It's been a long time since I said that. Come by the workshop. I'll make you a proper mug.
The deed is mine. The clay pits are mine. Father's promise... honored at last.
Brand's lawyers are at the gate. The kiln workers are striking. Edric is in chains.
Jory's here. Says we'd make a good team. Business and... more.
We'll see. The kiln fires burn hotter now. But the village square is quieter.
Was it worth it? Ask me in a year.
The ledger? Oh, Edric mentioned it. Said it turned up. Accounting error, he claimed.
The pottery's steady. Kiln's steady. Life goes on.
Jory's been... persistent. Comes by with 'found' clay samples. Charming, in his way.
Edric and I... we spoke. Briefly. At the well. He bought me a drink at the tavern.
Baby steps. That's how it goes, isn't it?
You're asking about the ledger? Edric's ledger?
Everyone in this village has something written in that book. Debts, promises, secrets.
Mara owes me for the herbs I gave her when the fever took her apprentice.
Jory... Jory brought me a letter he found in the kiln ruins. Burnt edges.
It mentioned a name — Edric's father. And a promise about the clay pits.
The truth heals. Slowly. Painfully. But it heals.
Edric confessed. Mara got her birthright. The village didn't burn.
Some medicines are bitter. This one... this one might actually work.
Come by anytime. The door's always open. For you, and for them.
Mara won. The pits are hers. Edric's gone.
But look around. The kiln's closing. Half the village is unemployed.
Jory's moving into the pottery. That's... a choice.
Healing isn't just about fixing what's broken. It's about what grows in the scar tissue.
We'll see what grows here.
You burned it. The ledger. In my fireplace.
I didn't stop you. Some truths... they're not medicine. They're poison.
Edric's still reeve. Brand still owns the kiln. Mara still thinks she failed.
The village goes on. Quiet. Whole. Built on a lie.
Was it the right choice? That's not my place to say. I just tend the wounds.
Even the ones you can't see.
Looking for the ledger? Might be I've seen it. Might be it's buried under a pile of scrap.
Edric thinks he's clever, using me to hide his dirty work. But I'm not his dog.
That ledger? It's insurance. If I give it to you, what's in it for me?
The pottery's clay pits would be worth a fortune to the right buyer.
Mara... she doesn't know what she's sitting on.
You'd do that? Help me claim the clay pits? Fine.
The ledger's in the old shrine, under the loose stone by the altar.
But if Mara gets those pits... she'll need someone to work them.
Someone who knows the land. Someone like me.
We'd make a good team, her and I. Better than she knows.
Careful. Mara's got enough on her plate without you stirring that pot.
But fine — you want the ledger? It's at the old shrine. Under the altar stone. Take it.
But know this: if Mara loses those pits because of you, I'll make sure everyone knows who really broke the promise.
It wasn't just Edric.
A council. No reeve. No single power. Clever.
Mara got the pits. Edric stepped down. Brand's lawyers went home empty-handed.
I didn't get the pits. But I got something else — a seat at the table.
Mara and me... we're figuring it out. Business partners. Maybe more.
Bellwater's changing. Might even survive it.
Told you we'd make a good team.
Mara's got the pits. I've got the know-how. Brand's got nothing but lawsuits.
Edric's gone. The kiln's reopening under new management. Our management.
The village square's quiet, sure. But the workshop? The workshop's roaring.
Come by anytime. First drink's on me.
You burned it. Smart. Or stupid. Time'll tell.
Edric's still reeve. Brand still owns the kiln. Mara still doesn't know.
I still have the other copy. The one I made before you found the original.
Insurance, remember?
Mara... she's worth waiting for. The pits are worth waiting for.
Bellwater isn't going anywhere. Neither am I.
Business is business, friend. The village owed me. Edric paid.
The kiln lease is legal. Binding. Signed and witnessed.
If the potter wants the clay pits... she can buy them. At market rate.
Which, coincidentally, is exactly what the village can't afford.
Now, if you'll excuse me — I have a kiln to run.
A council. How quaint. How... democratic.
The courts will hear my case. The lease is legal. My lawyers are already drafting the writ.
But... the village rallied. The blacksmith testified. Even the tavern keep spoke against me.
Fine. I'll negotiate. New terms. Fair terms.
But don't think this makes us friends. Business is business.
The potter has the deed. My lawyers are already at the village hall.
The kiln workers struck. My own workers. Ungrateful.
Edric's in chains. Good. He broke our contract.
This village will learn. You don't cross Brand Kiln Co.
We'll see who's still standing when the dust settles.
The ledger's gone. How... convenient.
Edric's still reeve. The lease stands. The kiln runs.
Business continues. As it should.
You're a practical sort. I like that. Maybe we'll do business someday.
Now run along. The kiln doesn't run itself.
Mara and I grew up together. She was always the dreamer. I was the one who stayed.
Edric... he was different then. Before the debt, before Brand. He cared.
Jory comes by the farm sometimes. Brings 'gifts.' Scrap metal, mostly. Once a carved wooden bird.
I don't know what to do with him. Or any of this.
The grain's nearly ready. That's what I know. The rest... that's for people like you to figure out.
Mara got the pits. Edric admitted the truth. The village... we're talking again.
Jory came by yesterday. Not with scrap. With a proper plow share. Forged by Tomas, he said.
Mara laughed when I told her. Actually laughed. First time in years.
The harvest will be good this year. I can feel it.
Mara won. The pits are hers. But the kiln's closing, Anna.
Half the village works that kiln. Their wages feed families. Buy my grain.
Jory's at the pottery now. Partner, he says. In everything.
Mara looks... tired. Proud, but tired.
I'll plant the winter crop. That's what I do. But I'm scared for what comes after.
Nothing changed. Edric's still reeve. Brand still owns the kiln. Mara still works the pottery.
Jory still brings me scrap metal. I still don't know what to do with him.
The grain's ready. The harvest comes in. Life goes on.
Maybe that's enough. Maybe it's not.
But the grain doesn't care about promises. It just grows.
Pull up a stool. The ale's decent, the gossip's better.
You want to know about the ledger? Everyone does. Nobody asks directly.
Edric and Mara — siblings who don't speak. Three years now.
Brand owns the kiln, but the clay pits... that's the real prize.
Jory knows things. He always knows things. Scavenger finds more than scrap.
Elara knows the rest. She's the healer. People tell healers what they won't tell priests.
What'll it be? Ale? Information? Both?
Well, well. The reeve confessed, the potter got her pits, the kiln master got humbled.
Best entertainment this tavern's seen in twenty years.
Drinks are on the house tonight. Courtesy of the new council — once they form it.
Tomas, my brother, he's already arguing with Brand's lawyers at the next table.
Bellwater's changing. Might even be for the better.
Mara won. Edric's gone. Brand's suing. The kiln's striking.
My brother Tomas says the blacksmith orders are drying up without the kiln's lime.
Jory's partner at the pottery now. He's been buying rounds all night.
Mara hasn't had a drink. Just sits there, staring at the deed.
Business is good tonight. But the mood... the mood is thin.
Same as always. Edric's reeve. Brand's kiln runs. Mara's pottery fires burn.
Jory and I... we have an understanding. He doesn't ask where I get my information.
I don't ask where he gets his ledgers.
Another ale? On the house. For a traveler who knows when to listen and when to forget.
Iron doesn't lie. You heat it, hammer it, it shows you what it is.
Brand's lime... good quality. Consistent. That's what matters in the forge.
Edric's a good reeve. Keeps the peace. Keeps the kiln running.
Mara's pottery... fine work. Buys my brackets, my hinges.
Jory's scrap... mostly useless. But sometimes he finds good steel.
My brother runs the tavern. We don't talk much. Different worlds.
What do you need forged?
I testified. In the square. Told them the kiln's lime was good but the lease was rotten.
Cost me the kiln contract. Brand canceled it the next day.
But my iron's still true. My word's still good.
Mara's pottery needs brackets. Hinges. I'll make them fair.
The village council... maybe it'll work. Maybe it won't. But it's honest.
Kiln's closed. Brand's lawyers tied it up in court.
No lime means no flux. No flux means bad welds. Bad welds mean broken tools.
Mara's got the pits. She's sending lime — but it's not the same. Not yet.
My brother's tavern's full of unemployed kiln workers. Drinking on credit.
I'm forging plow shares for Anna's farm. Payment in grain. It'll do.
Kiln runs. Lime flows. Forge burns hot.
Edric's reeve. Brand's lease holds. Mara's pottery buys my brackets.
Jory's scrap pile grows. Sometimes there's good steel in it.
Tomas at the tavern pours my ale. We don't talk. Don't need to.
Iron doesn't lie. The village stands. That's enough.
Welcome! Clay pots from Mara, lime from Brand, grain from Anna — I stock it all.
Business has been... interesting lately. Lots of whispers. Fewer customers.
Mara's pottery sells well. Tourists love the 'authentic Bellwater ware.'
Brand's kiln supplies half the region's lime. Big money. Big influence.
Edric keeps the peace. Mostly. The ledger... everyone knows it exists. Nobody talks about it.
Jory's scavenged goods — some real treasures mixed in with the junk.
What can I get you?
Business is booming! Mara's new pottery line — 'Reclaimed Clay' — selling like hotcakes.
Brand agreed to supply lime at a fair rate. The kiln's reopening Monday.
Edric's on the new council. So is Mara. So is Tomas. Even Jory got a seat — 'Salvage & Reclamation.'
Anna's grain harvest was record-breaking. I'm expanding the store!
Bellwater's on the map now. Literally — new trade route through the river bridge.
Mara's pottery is the talk of the region. 'Reclaimed Clay' — clever branding.
But Brand's lawsuit... the kiln's closed. Lime prices doubled.
Tomas the blacksmith can't get flux. Anna's grain isn't moving — no wagons from the kiln.
Jory's running the pottery's business side now. Sharp operator. Keeps asking for credit terms.
Edric's gone. The reeve's seat is empty. The council hasn't formed yet.
I'm... worried. But Mara's pottery is beautiful. Maybe beauty pays the bills.
Same suppliers. Same customers. Same gossip.
Mara's pots. Brand's lime. Anna's grain. Tomas's iron. Jory's... curiosities.
Edric keeps the ledger balanced. The village keeps breathing.
Profit margins are thin but steady. That's the shopkeeper's dream, isn't it?
Nothing changes. Everything changes. The ledger knows the difference.
Wood's wood. Trees don't care about ledgers or promises.
Brand's kiln burns through cordwood like a furnace. Keeps me busy.
Jory scavenges the offcuts. Says he 'processes' them. Vulture work.
Mara's pottery... she uses the ash for glaze. Smart. Waste not.
Edric leaves the woods alone. That's all I ask from a reeve.
Now if you'll excuse me, there's a stand of oak calling my name.
Edric told the truth. Mara got the pits. Brand backed down.
The kiln's reopening. New terms. Sustainable cut — they finally listened.
Jory's hauling clay now, not scrap. Says the pay's better.
The woods... they'll recover. We'll plant where we cut. Proper rotation.
Good work. For an outsider.
Kiln's closed. Brand's lawyers. No work for woodcutters.
Jory's at the pottery now. Says he's 'diversifying.'
Mara's clay pits... they need timber for the kilns. She's buying from me direct now.
Better price than Brand paid. But half the volume.
The woods are quiet. Too quiet. Trees falling with no one to hear them.
Kiln burns. I cut. Ax swings. Simple.
Ledgers, promises, lawyers... that's town talk.
Jory still scavenges. Mara still pots. Edric still reeves. Brand still brands.
The oak stand's ready. Been waiting thirty years.
Wood doesn't lie. Neither does the axe.
